content:
The image shows a soybean leaf with numerous small, scattered yellow-green spots distributed across the upper leaf surface. The spots are tiny, roughly circular, and light yellow-green against the darker green leaf background. No brown lesions, pustules, or necrosis are visible yet — these appear to be early-stage lesions.

Key observations:
- Upper leaf surface
- Many small, discrete yellow-green spots scattered across the leaf
- No angular vein-limited lesions (rules out Bacterial_Blight)
- No water-soaking visible
- No gray centers with reddish borders (rules out Frogeye)
- No purplish margins (rules out Phyllosticta or Septoria at this stage)
- Spots are light green/yellow, small, and numerous — consistent with early Downy Mildew, which starts as small light green spots on upper leaf surfaces

Downy mildew description: "Small light green spots on upper leaf surfaces that enlarge and turn pale to bright yellow." This matches very well — the spots are small, light green/yellow, scattered on the upper surface.

Bacterial pustule also shows small light green spots, but those develop raised centers/pustules, which are not clearly visible here.

These scattered tiny yellow-green spots on the upper leaf surface most closely match the early stage of Downy Mildew.
